meta.title: Nuvistela: a real-life adventure
meta.description: Complete a small real-life activity and unlock the next chapter of an AI-assisted story, on your own or with people you care about.
meta.ogTitle: Nuvistela: a family adventure game · free
meta.ogDescription: Real-life deeds unlock chapters of your own story. No sign-up, no email: start playing in a minute, solo or with the whole family.
meta.ogImageAlt: Colourful artwork: a family on a rainbow path through the fairy-tale world of Nuvistela

landing.title: A story starring you, where real-life deeds unlock each chapter
landing.pitch: Tidy a room, take a walk, finish a book — an AI storyteller continues a story about you. Solo or with your family.
landing.trust: No email or account needed: a game title, your name and a couple of interests are enough.

steps.d: On your own or with people you care about: say who is taking part and what each person loves. The heroes and the story world are drawn for you.
Tidying up, a walk, a hobby: the game master suggests a small real-life activity that suits you, and each age if children take part.

steps.t: Mark it done, get the next chapter
steps.d: On your own, you mark it yourself; together, someone else can confirm. The story continues with a new chapter and a next activity.

p: Nuvistela is a family game: adults and children complete small tasks at home together, and the story of the world is written from their check-ins. The personal data operator is sole proprietor [operator name] (OGRNIP [OGRNIP], INN [INN], Russia). For questions about your data, write to privacy@example.com.
- The family name and the names or nicknames of the players that you enter. You may give a nickname instead of a real name.
- The age group of each player (3–5, 6–9, 10–13, 14–17 or adult) and their interests, if you provided them.
- Your check-ins on completed tasks and your messages in the chat with the game master.
- The history of the world: the tasks, chapters, covers and 3D scenes created for your family.
- If you connected Telegram: the chat identifier and the texts the bot receives and sends in that chat.
- If you turned on notifications: your browser's subscription address and time zone.
- If you previously submitted a pilot request: your email address, family size, the age groups of the children and language.
- Usage events (for example, "task completed") linked to the family, without names or text; they are erased together with the family.
- Technical request data (IP address, browser) in web server logs, needed to protect against abuse.
We do not ask for photographs, addresses, phone numbers or documents, and we do not use children's data for advertising. There are no third-party counters or advertising trackers on the site.

To run your family's game: to devise tasks, write chapters and pictures of the world, remind you about a new task if you want that, and contact you about a pilot request submitted earlier. The basis is your consent, which you give when creating the family, and the performance of the agreement on using the game.

A family is created by an adult. By creating it, the adult confirms that they are the parent or legal representative of the children they add and consents to the processing of their data. A child enters the game only by invitation from this adult.

The texts of stories and tasks and the pictures are written by artificial intelligence models. We pass them only what is needed for a particular chapter or picture, and we forbid model providers to store the requests or to train on them.

- **OpenRouter** (USA): access to language and image models. Names are not passed into chapters and descriptions of the world: they are replaced with a label. The game master in the chat sees the family name and the players' names in order to address you. Descriptions for pictures are cleared of names, ages and interests.
- **World Labs** (USA): 3D scenes of the world. Only the description of the scene is passed, without names; the scene is closed to public access.
- **Telegram**: if you connected the bot, the messages in your chat.
- **Browser notification services** (Google, Apple, Mozilla, Microsoft, depending on the browser): the text of the reminder, sent to the subscription address.
- **HOSTKEY** (Finland, the Netherlands): the servers on which the data is stored.
Some of these companies are located outside your country of residence. We do not sell data to anyone.
An adult can create a public link to a world card. Anyone who has the link can see it; players' names are not shown on the card. The link can be revoked at any time.
- `bumbli_session`: signs you in to the family, for up to 365 days.
- `NEXT_LOCALE`: the language you chose.
- Browser storage: which world events you have already seen, the world cover, the refusal of notifications, and service keys that prevent one check-in from being sent twice.

Family data is kept for as long as the family exists. The family owner can delete it in the "Family" section: the players, tasks, chapters, pictures, 3D scenes, links, subscriptions and Telegram bindings are deleted. A pilot request submitted earlier will be deleted on request to privacy@example.com. The accounting of model costs retains only amounts, with no link to the family.

You can find out what data we keep, correct it, delete the family, withdraw your consent (this means deleting the family) and decline notifications. Write to privacy@example.com and we will reply within 10 working days. You also have the right to apply to the personal data protection authority of your country.
If the policy changes, a new date and version will appear on this page. We will notify you in the game of any material changes.
